fieldNotes.siteResolution: Original approximate coords (43.0710,-73.7846) landed ~3km NE on a cemetery. Web search confirmed the Saratoga Spring Water Company / BlueTriton (now Primo Brands) bottling plant at 11 Geyser Road (Route 29), Saratoga Springs NY 12866 - founded 1872, the oldest continuously bottling water company at the same site. Resolved address point 43.0587,-73.8105; satellite confirmed a compact industrial bottling complex (silver/blue metal warehouse NW + older gray/blue bottling-process buildings center/SE) on the north side of Geyser Road, with the Kayaderosseras Creek to the east. Locked plant/yard center 43.05895,-73.81095.
fieldNotes.truckGate: FALSE - definitive. The single main truck driveway opens directly off Geyser Road as a wide-open paved curb cut with NO barrier arm, NO sliding/swing gate, and NO checkpoint pinch-point. Street View (pano DsolxoLUGNLjF2lNdtVaeA, 2022-03) headings 0/25/340 all show an open apron into the yard; a green-painted directional/one-way marking is present but is not a physical control.
fieldNotes.guardShack: FALSE - definitive. No booth-sized structure (1-3 vehicle footprint, multi-side windows) anywhere at the entrance in Street View or satellite. The nearest structure to the entrance is the blue metal warehouse itself.
fieldNotes.remoteGs: FALSE - no truck gate exists, so no remote/kiosk check-in applies.
fieldNotes.fencing: The rear (NW/west) trailer-storage lot is enclosed by chain-link perimeter fencing (visible in the far-west Street View pano n5QU41fdyM2INP7UXhggTw), but the active truck entrance off Geyser Road is uncontrolled and open.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: Modest dock line under a canopy along the SE face of the NW warehouse building; z21 imagery shows a single trailer backed in plus a continuous low canopy suggesting ~4-8 doors. Banded 0-10. Some loading also occurs at the older bottling building via the central paved apron. Low-confidence count given the canopy obscures individual door rhythm.
fieldNotes.dropArea: West storage lot holds a diagonal cluster of ~8-9 trailers/storage containers without tractors (p32-trailers-w.png). Banded 0-10.
fieldNotes.dropYard: TRUE - the fenced west lot is a distinct trailer/container storage area separate from the active dock apron.
fieldNotes.postGateStaging: Large open paved apron between the warehouse, the bottling building, and the creek serves as an internal queue/turn-around and staging area inside the property.
fieldNotes.drivewayLong: The open yard between the road entrance and the dock/apron easily holds a queue of 3+ trucks before they reach the docks; the property is deep relative to its frontage.
fieldNotes.entryExitTogether: One driveway off Geyser Road serves both entry and exit; the green-painted one-way markings split lanes within that single curb cut.
fieldNotes.scale: No truck scale / weigh pad visible in the truck path. FALSE.
fieldNotes.shipRcvSeparate: Single dock cluster on the warehouse SE face; loading at the older bottling building appears informal via the shared apron. Could not confirm physically separate ship/receive banks - marked FALSE, low confidence.
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: One contiguous bottling complex (warehouse + connected process buildings), not a multi-cluster campus. FALSE.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Edge-of-town setting on State Route 29 west of Saratoga Springs, bordered by woods, a creek, and scattered houses. Rural per the rubric (small-town/edge-of-town industrial).
fieldNotes.connectivityIssue: Site sits on a state highway with adjacent residential development and a town nearby; cellular coverage is unlikely to be a problem. FALSE.
fieldNotes.railServed: No rail spur enters the property. FALSE.
fieldNotes.siteAreaAcres: ~6.5 acres of cleared/paved/built footprint inside the property line, derived from the perimeter polygon; compact legacy plant, much smaller than a modern DC.
fieldNotes.buildingCount: Three distinct structures: the silver/blue metal warehouse (NW), the older gray-roofed bottling/process building (center), and the connected blue process/office section fronting the road (SE) - counted as 3.
